title: Mindy Kaling Tests Hailey Bieber's Viral Protein Pizza and Gives It Her Stamp of Approval
excerpt: The actress and writer shared her kitchen experiment on Instagram, complete with moments of doubt, a 'Bieber SOS,' and an enthusiastic final verdict.
body:
• Mindy Kaling tested Hailey Bieber's viral cottage cheese protein pizza recipe in an Instagram Reel, calling it 'so good' after initial skepticism
  • The recipe uses cottage cheese, egg whites, flour, coconut flour and baking powder for a high-protein pizza crust
  • Kaling, who has been open about her fitness journey, said she's 'always trying to get in that extra protein for my heavy lifting'

Doubt, Then Delight

Mindy Kaling is the latest celebrity to take on one of this year's most viral recipes — and she did it with the kind of honest, self-deprecating energy her fans have come to expect.

The actress, writer and producer shared an Instagram Reel of herself making Hailey Bieber's cottage cheese protein pizza, a recipe that has swept social media since the Rhode founder posted it earlier this year. "I'm so excited because today we are doing a viral recipe," Kaling says in the video. "It's the Hailey Bieber protein pizza recipe that I keep seeing online."

The result? A genuine endorsement — but not before some entertaining moments of culinary panic.

The Recipe

The cottage cheese protein pizza swaps traditional dough for a high-protein base made with cottage cheese, egg whites, regular flour, coconut flour and baking powder, seasoned with salt, garlic powder and oregano. The mixture is spread on a baking sheet, baked until set, then topped with marinara, mozzarella and fresh basil before going back in the oven.

Kaling followed the steps faithfully but wasn't immediately convinced. "That doesn't seem like, very dough-like," she says while mixing the ingredients. As she flattened the mixture onto the baking sheet, she admitted: "It smells really good, but looking at the little pieces of cottage cheese is kind of gross."

The Bieber SOS

The first 10-minute bake didn't look right. "Still looks pretty raw," Kaling said, putting it back in the oven for extra time — a departure from the original instructions. "Hailey, please comment if we're doing the right thing," she pleaded, as on-screen text read: "Sending out a Bieber SOS."

The extended bake time paid off. When she finally pulled out the finished pizza — complete with toasted cheese and browned edges — the verdict was immediate.

"Oh my gosh, this is great. I was kind of dubious, but this is so good. Hailey Bieber, you have done it again."

— Mindy Kaling

"The @haileybieber protein pizza recipe was a real lesson in trusting the process honestly!!!" Kaling wrote in her Instagram caption. Fans were persuaded. "Alright I'll try it you got me," one commenter wrote.

The Protein Priority

Kaling's interest in the recipe aligns with her public focus on health and fitness. "I really want to try it because I'm always trying to get in that extra protein for my heavy lifting," she says in the video, before cutting to a gym photo with the self-aware aside, "Actually that's kind of true."

The mother of three has been candid about her weight loss journey in recent interviews. Speaking on The View in May while promoting her Hulu series Not Suitable for Work, Kaling addressed the public's reaction directly: "I have wanted to lose weight since I was 12 years old. I've been writing jokes about diet and body image for 20 years now."

She emphasized that health, not aesthetics alone, drives the effort. "My mom died young of cancer and both my parents had diabetes. I need to live. I need to live and the kids need me," she said. Kaling sees a trainer three times a week and closely watches her diet.

Worth Trying at Home

The cottage cheese protein pizza has become one of the most-shared high-protein meal ideas of the year, part of a broader trend of using cottage cheese as a versatile base for everything from pancakes to pizza crusts. Kaling's entertaining, relatable take on the recipe — complete with genuine skepticism and a willingness to deviate from the instructions — may be exactly what convinces the next wave of home cooks to give it a shot.
